nodes.title: The cubic wild types
nodes.statement: Fix an order-three matrix ζ in GL₂(Z₃). The Q₃-type τ₁ is the two-dimensional inertia representation corresponding by arithmetic reciprocity to the character of Z₃× with values −1↦1 and 4↦ζ. The type τ₋₁ is the representation obtained from the unramified quadratic field Q₃(j), j²=−1, whose unit character has values 4j↦1, 4↦1 and 1+3j↦ζ. These specify isomorphism classes, not chosen matrices or a finite-image Weil representation. Extend the inertia classes to Weil representations as in the supplier’s type definition.

proofSteps: Compute the relevant unit quotients using local reciprocity; the listed generators and relations determine the characters.
View the Q₃ character over its quadratic coefficient field as a two-dimensional representation; use induction/restriction for the unramified quadratic case.
Conjugating the order-three matrix replaces the realization without changing the type class.
acceptance: Both inertia images have order three; τ₋₁ has the nontrivial Frobenius conjugation on its cubic inertia image.

nodes.title: The positive ramified quadratic field
nodes.statement: Let s²=3, j²=−1, α³−3α+3=0 and β²=s. Set F′₃=Q₃(s,j,α,β). It has degree 24, e=12 and f=2; over Q₃(s) it is the abelian extension of degree twelve whose norm subgroup is topologically generated by 3,4,1+3s. Let q∈1+3Z₃ satisfy q²=−5. Choose γ₃ fixing j and β and sending α to (−2sα²−(3s+q)α+4s)/(2q); γ₂ fixes α,β and negates j; γ₄ fixes α,j and takes β to jβ. γ₂²=γ₃³=γ₄⁴=1, γ₂γ₃=γ₃γ₂, γ₄γ₂=γ₂γ₄⁻¹ and γ₄γ₃=γ₃²γ₄; γ₄² has order TWO. The residue field is F₉, γ₂ acts on it by x↦x³, and γ₃,γ₄ act trivially on it. Put π=α/β and F₃=(F′₃)^{γ₂}=Q₃(π). Then π is a uniformizer. Its Eisenstein polynomial has form u¹²−3G(u), G(0)=1, cπ(0)=−1; Hγ₂=1, Hγ₄=−j, Hγ₃≡1+u² modulo (3,u⁴). For g,g′ in ⟨γ₂,γ₄⟩ the corrections tg and fg,g′ vanish.

nodes.title: Simple admittance for the cubic types
nodes.statement: For a continuous ρ̄:G₃→GL₂(F₃) whose inertia restriction is a très ramifié extension of ω by 1, both τ₁ and τ₋₁ simply admit ρ̄ in the exact BCDT §1.3 sense: there is a unique admitting Jordan–Hölder constituent, it occurs with multiplicity one, and that constituent simply admits ρ̄. nodes.statement: For all four pairs, Θ₀=0 on Ext¹_{Sᵢ,(r,s)}(ρ̄,ρ̄). For the three nonexceptional pairs, Θ₁=0 when r≠6 and Θω=0 when s≠6. For (6,6), Θω=0. In particular on every fixed-determinant category tangent both the required lower-left and a diagonal inertia comparison vanish.

proofSteps: For the three nonexceptional pairs use reversed Ext vanishing to kill Θ₀ and an extreme-weight diagonal Ext calculation to kill the indicated diagonal.
For (6,6) the rank-three filtration has u⁶eω,u⁶e′₁+(b+b′u⁴)eω,u⁶e′ω+(c+c′u⁴)e′₁+f eω, with c≠0. Containment of u¹²M in the filtration forces b=b′=0 and kills Θ₀.

The resulting diagonal extension has only the u⁶ parameter and is unramified by extended-diagonal-extensions. The matrix calculation uses only the integral self-extension and c≠0, so also gives the all-self-extension formulation of Theorem 4.7.5.

nodes.title: Compatible characteristic-three Artin deformations
nodes.statement: For (r,s)=(2,6),(6,10),(2,10), take the residual parameters (c,c₁), with c₁≠0 for a très extension, and t=2,6,8 respectively. For N≥1 put A_N=F₃[T]/(Tᴺ) and construct the rank-two Breuil module over A_N[u]/u³⁶ with filtration ⟨uˢe₁,uʳe′ω+(c+T)uᵗe₁⟩, φ₁ sending these generators to e₁,e′ω, and N=0. Its Frobenius is A_N-linear and sends u to u³, fixing T; descent is exactly that of extended-models with the same c₁. The corresponding finite-flat descent model has special-fibre F=0 and gives a free rank-two A_N generic representation ρ_N with determinant ω, reducing to ρ̄ at T=0. Choose compatible generic bases for the reductions A_N→A_M. For N≥2 its reduction modulo T² is the nontrivial deformation ρ₂, not the constant extension ρ̄⊗A₂.

proofSteps: Substitute c+T into the three normal forms, using an A_N-linear u-Frobenius. Check corrected descent, Frobenius generation, the ideal and zero special-fibre F.
For 1≤M<N, multiplication by T^{N−M} gives 0→M_M→M_N→M_{N−M}→0 in the exact Breuil category. Contravariant generic fibre and order counts prove freeness over A_N and residual compatibility.
The rank-one generic pieces are A_N(ω) and A_N, so the determinant is ω. Lift bases compatibly through the nilpotent reduction maps.
At N=2 use the two rank-one comparison maps in §9.5 and its nonsplit rank-two subquotient with filtration cross term uᵗ. The generic Ext isomorphism proves the resulting self-extension is nontrivial.

nodes.title: The three purely characteristic-three deformation rings
nodes.statement: For each i and each nonexceptional pair, R^{ε,Sᵢ,(r,s)}_{V,Z₃}≅F₃[[T]] as complete local Z₃-algebras. In particular the WHOLE ring is killed by three, not only its special fibre. It has no characteristic-zero points.

proofSteps: The tangent upper bound and compatible nontrivial A_N deformations for every N imply R/(3)≅F₃[[T]]. Generic-fibre uniqueness of the strong-filtered model makes special-fibre F=0 for every Artinian quotient of R/(3).

For an arbitrary Artinian quotient of R, use the supplied integral exact realization of its generic groups 3G and G/3G. On its contravariant Dieudonné module D the image of the multiplication-by-three composite is 3D, and the embedded module of G/3G is ker(3:D→D).

F kills that kernel because G/3G belongs to the mod-three family, and V_D=−F from Iᵢ, so F²=−3. For x killed by nine, 3Fx=F(3x)=0; hence Fx lies in ker 3 and F²x=0, giving 3x=0. Thus D[9]=D[3]. Finite three-primary length now implies 3D=0.

Faithfulness of Dieudonné and integral generic-fibre realization give 3G=0, and freeness of the generic rank-two representation gives 3R=0 for every Artinian quotient. Pass to the complete ring. This annihilator argument avoids an unjustified lift of endomorphisms from 3D in the printed proof.
acceptance: Residual F=0 by itself is not used to conclude 3R=0: the argument controls ker 3 at an arbitrary Artinian level.

At the first coefficient-uniformizer torsion level apply extended-coefficient-filtration. The supplied weak-to-strong criteria give filtration by its rank-one pieces, then by one Gᵢ,(r,s).
All successive coefficient-torsion layers have that same residual model, so all finite levels satisfy the same category deformation condition.
A characteristic-zero point cannot factor through one of the three rings killed by three. Therefore it uses (6,6); intersect type-point kernels to obtain the quotient factorization.

nodes.title: A global companion with prescribed local three-torsion
nodes.statement: Let ρ:G_Q→GL₂(F₅) be continuous with determinant the mod-five cyclotomic character. Choose its alternating pairing into μ₅ to agree, after an equivariant local identification, with the Weil pairing of the local companion E₁/Q₃. On the fixed-pairing twist Y_ρ(5), the point (E₁,α) has a nonempty 3-adic open neighborhood U on which the full G₃-module E_x[3] is isomorphic to E₁[3]. There is (E,β)∈Y_ρ(5)(Q)∩U, where β:ρ≅E[5] preserves the chosen pairing, and G_Q→Aut(E[3]) is surjective. The curve E has the same full local three-torsion as E₁. Absolute irreducibility of ρ is not required for this construction.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.2.1, p.864; Shepherd-Barron–Taylor §1, Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.2, pp.285–286; Manoharmayum §2.2, p.738

proofSteps: Use the fixed-pairing moduli twist and the supplied rational compactification X_ρ(5)≅P¹_Q. Remove its finitely many cusps; the universal elliptic curve exists on this fine moduli open.
Use local constancy of finite étale three-torsion to choose U retaining the full G₃-representation and its ramification, not merely inertia semisimplification.

Apply Hilbert irreducibility with the 3-adic open condition to the degree-24 cover of ordered independent three-torsion pairs (a,b) modulo (a,b)~(−a,b). Its geometric model is the fixed-pairing level-fifteen curve, hence it is geometrically connected. A specialization of full fibre degree gives image of order at least 24. GL₂(F₃) has just one subgroup of index two, SL₂(F₃), so that image contains SL₂(F₃); its nontrivial cyclotomic determinant over Q then gives GL₂(F₃).

The universal five-torsion identification provides β and the selected point gives E[3]|G₃≅E₁[3]. The first-vector sign quotient exchanges the two possible pairing values and gives a geometrically connected cover over Q. Quotienting by simultaneous sign instead would leave two components; do not replace this cover by that quotient or assert a regular GL₂(F₃)-Galois cover.
acceptance: Surjectivity is on the global mod-three representation; local mod-three image is the prescribed one.
